Filter

dim(shap)
## [1] 18282     7
shap = data.matrix(shap)
to_keep = filter(new_rna, abs(prediction_error) < 0.5 &
                  abs(new_rna$logfc) > 0.5) %>% pull(promoter_id)
filtered = shap[to_keep,]
filtered = filtered[order(rowSums(filtered)),]
dim(filtered)
## [1] 4455    7
summary(filtered)

keep_white = filter(new_rna, abs(prediction_error) < 0.5 &
                  new_rna$logfc < -0.5) %>% pull(promoter_id)
length(keep_white)
## [1] 712
white = filtered[keep_white,]

keep_beige = filter(new_rna, abs(prediction_error) < 0.5 &
                  new_rna$logfc > 0.5) %>% pull(promoter_id)
length(keep_beige)
## [1] 3743
beige = shap[keep_beige,]
nrow(white); nrow(beige)
## [1] 712
## [1] 3743

Heatmap and clustering

clusters = list(white = hclust(as.dist(1-cor(t(white)))), beige = hclust(as.dist(1-cor(t(beige)))))
cluster_splits = list(white=cutree(clusters[["white"]], 6), beige = cutree(clusters[["beige"]], 6))
head(clusters)
## $white
## 
## Call:
## hclust(d = as.dist(1 - cor(t(white))))

## Number of objects: 712 
## 
## 
## $beige
## 
## Call:

col_fun = colorRamp2(c(-0.6, 0, 0.6), c("blue", "white", "red"))

I’ve done the plotting first with this pre-computed clusters (hclust on 1- pearon correlations). I checked splitting into 4 and 8 clusters and liked 8 the best for selecting small specific groups. So I pre-calculated the cluster splits using cutee cluster_splits. Then the heatmap is reordered inside the function which leads to the numbers being out of order on the plot - but this is fixable later. (the way complexheatmap orders the clusters is different to basic cutree)

h = Heatmap(data.matrix(white), show_row_names = F, cluster_row_slices = T,
        row_split = cluster_splits[["white"]], use_raster=T,
        col=col_fun, clustering_distance_rows = "pearson",  name= "SHAP value", row_dend_width = unit(30,"mm"))
h

pdf(here(figpath, "white_shap_heatmap_6clusters.pdf"))
h
dev.off()
## png 
##   2
Heatmap(data.matrix(white), cluster_rows = clusters[["white"]], show_row_names = F, row_split = 8, use_raster=T,
        col=col_fun, name= "SHAP value", row_dend_width = unit(30,"mm"))

Heatmap(data.matrix(white), cluster_rows = clusters[["white"]], show_row_names = F, row_split = 4, use_raster=T,
        col=col_fun, name= "SHAP value", row_dend_width = unit(30,"mm"))

h = Heatmap(data.matrix(beige), show_row_names = F,
        row_split = cluster_splits[["beige"]], use_raster=T,
        col=col_fun, clustering_distance_rows = "pearson",  name= "SHAP value", 
        row_dend_width = unit(30,"mm"), row_dend_reorder = cluster_splits[["beige"]])
h

pdf(here(figpath, "beige_shap_heatmap_6clusters.pdf"))
h
dev.off()

        col=col_fun,  name= "SHAP value", row_dend_width = unit(30,"mm"))

Heatmap(data.matrix(beige), cluster_rows = clusters[["beige"]], show_row_names = F, row_split = 10, use_raster=T,
        col=col_fun,  name= "SHAP value", row_dend_width = unit(30,"mm"))

Heatmap(data.matrix(beige), cluster_rows = clusters[["beige"]], show_row_names = F, row_split = 8, use_raster=T,
        col=col_fun,  name= "SHAP value", row_dend_width = unit(30,"mm"))

Heatmap(data.matrix(beige), cluster_rows = clusters[["beige"]], show_row_names = F, row_split = 4, use_raster=T,
        col=col_fun,  name= "SHAP value", row_dend_width = unit(30,"mm"))

Heatmap(filtered, show_row_names = F, row_split = 8, col=col_fun)

Heatmap(filtered, show_row_names = F, row_split = 4, col=col_fun, clustering_distance_rows = "pearson")

GO analysis on clusters

molsig <- clusterProfiler::read.gmt("/projects/imb-pkbphil/sp/annotations/molsigdb/msigdb.v2023.1.Hs.symbols.gmt")
head(molsig); nrow(molsig)
##      term       gene
## 1 chr1p11  LINC02798
## 2 chr1p11    MTIF2P1
## 3 chr1p11    SRGAP2C
## 4 chr1p11 SRGAP2-AS1
## 5 chr1p11  LINC01691
## 6 chr1p11     NBPF26
## [1] 3961711
prefixes = c("HALLMARK", "KEGG","REACTOME", "WP", "GOBP", "GOCC","GOMF")
colnames(molsig) = c("term","gene")
some.molsig = molsig[gsub("_.*","", molsig$term) %in% prefixes,]
some.molsig$term = factor(some.molsig$term)
table(gsub("_.*","", some.molsig$term))
## 
##     GOBP     GOCC     GOMF HALLMARK     KEGG REACTOME       WP 
##   642656    98915   108833     7322    12796    92769    31635
rm(molsig)

shorten = function(ont) {
  abbreviate(gsub("_"," ", tolower(ont)),minlength=40, dot=T, named = F)
}
wgoin = merge(new_rna, data.frame(cluster=cluster_splits[["white"]],
                         promoter_id=names(cluster_splits[["white"]])), 
      by = "promoter_id")
write.table(wgoin, here(sprintf("../clustering/white_clusters_%s_optimised_params.tsv", model_name)),
            sep="\t", row.names=F, quote=F)
